source: NASA NSSDCA lunar landing site coordinates; mission dates from NASA and CNSA/ISRO press material

sites.name: Luna 2
sites.blurb: The first human-made object to reach another world. It struck the Moon at 3.3 km/s, carrying pennants with the Soviet coat of arms.

sites.name: Surveyor 1
sites.blurb: America's first soft landing. Surveyor 1 sent home 11,237 photographs and proved the surface would hold a spacecraft.

sites.name: Apollo 11
sites.blurb: Tranquility Base. Armstrong and Aldrin spent 21 hours 36 minutes on the surface and brought back 21.5 kg of rock.

sites.name: Apollo 12
sites.blurb: A pinpoint landing 160 m from Surveyor 3, whose camera the crew retrieved and carried home.

sites.name: Apollo 14
sites.blurb: Shepard, the first American in space, hit two golf balls here with a makeshift six-iron.

sites.name: Apollo 15
sites.blurb: The first Lunar Roving Vehicle drove 27.9 km along a 300 m deep lava channel below the Apennine mountains.

sites.name: Apollo 16
sites.blurb: The only landing in the lunar highlands. The rocks turned out to be impact breccias, not volcanic as expected.

sites.name: Apollo 17
sites.blurb: The last footprints. Schmitt, a geologist, found orange volcanic glass; Cernan's were the final steps in December 1972.

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.blurb: The first robotic sample return: 101 grams of soil drilled and flown home without a single person aboard.

sites.name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
sites.blurb: The first wheeled vehicle on another world drove 10.5 km over 11 lunar days, steered from Earth.

sites.name: Chang'e 3
sites.blurb: China's first landing, carrying the Yutu rover. The first soft landing anywhere on the Moon since 1976.

sites.name: Chang'e 4
sites.blurb: The first landing on the far side, inside the South Pole-Aitken basin, relayed through the Queqiao satellite.

sites.name: Chang'e 5
sites.blurb: Returned 1.7 kg of the youngest lunar basalts ever sampled, just two billion years old.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3
sites.blurb: India's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover: the closest landing yet to the lunar south pole.

sites.name: SLIM
sites.blurb: Japan's pinpoint lander touched down within 100 m of its target, then toppled onto its nose and kept working.

sites.name: Odysseus (IM-1)
sites.blurb: The first commercial landing on the Moon, and the first US landing since Apollo 17.

sites.name: Blue Ghost M1
sites.blurb: Delivered ten NASA instruments and watched a total solar eclipse from the surface as Earth covered the Sun.
